title: Alasdair's small hulls
summary: On the strand below Seann Skell the boat-wright Alasdair mac Iain builds hulls no longer than his arm on spines of oak and floats them in the river pool and the river mouth, to learn what a keel does. He finds that a keel makes a hull stiff and lets it be built bigger.

title: Mòrag undertakes to pay for the oaks
summary: At Inis àrsaidh Mòrag nic Dhòmhnaill and Aonghas mac Fhionnlaigh hear Alasdair out and send him to look at the grove of Doire fhionn. Mòrag undertakes to pay for the felling and hauling out of her own silver.

title: The naming of the trees
summary: Eilidh nic Ruairidh, keeper of the grove of Doire fhionn, makes Alasdair choose each oak he will take and hear its name. He chooses fifty-four and leaves one young tree, the Child, standing alone.

title: The felling of the Queen
summary: Eighty men of the households of the roll fell the grove of Doire fhionn through the summer, each tree onto a bed of brush. The greatest, called the Queen, takes two days to bring down.

title: The ox-sleds on the north road
summary: The keel-timbers are dragged forty-two miles south to the sea on sleds of oak shod with ash, six yoke to a sled. The road is widened at every bend and a causeway built over the stream below Doire fhionn.

title: Woodcutters' huts at Doire fhiadhaich
summary: Woodcutters of the roll build huts at the edge of a wild oak wood on the shore of Loch chrom to fell crooked oak for the fleet's frames and knees. They go home when the felling is done and the huts fall in; the wood keeps its name.

title: The bed of the first keel
summary: Alasdair levels a line of oak blocks on the strand above the high-water mark and digs a saw-pit beside it. The Queen oak is rolled onto the blocks and hewn to a keel with a ridge along its underside.

title: Coinneach mac Fhearghais sworn
summary: At the feast of Lugh the wrights of the strand bind themselves into one fellowship. A custodian of Taigh na Fèithe swears their apprentices over a coal, and the first sworn is Coinneach mac Fhearghais, a coaster-wright's son of fourteen.

title: The first frames stand on the strand
summary: By the moon of Pailteach the first frames rise from the keel in pairs, pegged with heart-oak. The harbour scribe writes that the hull looks like the ribs of a great beast picked clean on the shore.

title: The Child walled
summary: The village of Doire fhionn builds a low wall of stones round the one young oak left on the grove hill, and its old keeper sits beside it every evening until dark.

title: Alasdair walks north with a knotted line
summary: In the moon of Gearras, after Là Fhèill Brìde, Alasdair mac Iain sets out alone on the north road with a pack, a staff and a line knotted every arm's length for measuring, making fifteen miles the first day and sleeping in a byre.
